raw_case_text:
A 72-year-old male farmer with no prior medical history presented to our emergency room with fever and bilateral calf pain for 3 days, followed by hemoptysis for 1 day. Upon arrival at the emergency room, the patient experienced respiratory distress and orthopnea, with a body temperature of 38.6 C, respiratory rate of 30 breaths/min, pulse rate of 129 beats/min, and blood pressure of 129/70 mmHg. With an oxygen mask at 8 L/min, the oxygen saturation was 89%. Chest CT revealed bilateral pulmonary exudative changes (Figure 2A). His initial lab results were: P/F, 124 mmHg; PLT, 12 x 109/L; CRP, 219.72 mg/L; PCT, 74.68 ng/mL; APTT, 30 s; MYO, >2000 ng/mL; CR, 128 mg/dL; ALT, 98 U/L; TBIL, 64.1 mumol/L. The primary diagnosis included severe pneumonia, DAH, severe ARDS, and hepatic and renal dysfunction.
The patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated with 100% FiO2 support, but his P/F declined to 66 mmHg. Emergency VV-ECMO and CRRT support were initiated, along with intermittent prone ventilation. He remained on volume-controlled ventilation (tidal volume 200-300 mL, PEEP 20 cmH2O, plateau pressure <=35 mmHg). Empirical antibiotic therapy included moxifloxacin (0.4 g IV daily) combined with imipenem/cilastatin (1 g IV every 8 h). The patient also received methylprednisolone (500 mg IV for 3 days), recombinant human thrombopoietin (15,000 U SC daily), fresh plasma, packed red blood cells, norepinephrine (0.1-1.2 mug/kg/min), and bronchoscopic alveolar lavage. Both blood and lavage fluid were sent for mNGS testing. On day 3, mNGS confirmed leptospirosis, and platelet transfusion (10 U) was administered on day 4, but a follow-up chest CT showed worsening pulmonary hemorrhage (Figure 2B). On day 11, VV-ECMO was discontinued, and a follow-up chest CT showed significant improvement in pulmonary hemorrhage (Figure 2C). The total duration of VV-ECMO support was 255 h, with the first 60 h without UFH anticoagulation. On day 15, the endotracheal tube was removed. On day 17, the patient was transferred out of the EICU. On day 21, the patient was discharged after recovery. A follow-up chest CT before discharge showed that pulmonary hemorrhage had significantly improved (Figure 2D). The treatment process is summarized in Figure 2E, and the trends in blood test results are detailed in Table 3. Changes in ventilator parameters, ECMO parameters, and medication dosages during ECMO are detailed in Table 2.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 72-year-old male presenting with fever and bilateral calf pain for 3 days, followed by hemoptysis and dyspnea for 1 day.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Symptoms began 3 days prior to presentation with acute fever and prominent bilateral calf pain. One day prior to admission, he developed frank hemoptysis, severe respiratory distress, and orthopnea, prompting emergency room presentation. Following admission, his oxygenation rapidly deteriorated despite endotracheal intubation, precipitating severe ARDS and multiorgan dysfunction.
subjective.past_medical_history: No prior medical history. Occupation: farmer. Epidemiological exposures: farm work; specific animal or water exposures not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports fever, severe bilateral calf pain, hemoptysis, orthopnea, and dyspnea. Home medications: none. Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Upon emergency presentation: acute respiratory distress and orthopnea. Body temperature 38.6 °C, respiratory rate 30 breaths/min, pulse rate 129 beats/min, blood pressure 129/70 mmHg. Oxygen saturation 89% on an 8 L/min oxygen mask.
objective.routine_investigations: PaO2/FiO2 ratio 124 mmHg initially, falling to 66 mmHg on 100% FiO2 following mechanical ventilation. Platelet count 12 x 10^9/L. C-reactive protein 219.72 mg/L. Procalcitonin 74.68 ng/mL. APTT 30 s. Serum myoglobin >2000 ng/mL. Serum creatinine 128 mg/dL [or mcmol/L as reported]. ALT 98 U/L. Total bilirubin 64.1 mcmol/L.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial chest CT: bilateral pulmonary exudative changes. Follow-up chest CT on day 4: worsening pulmonary hemorrhage. Follow-up chest CT on day 11 and before discharge (day 21): significant improvement and near-complete resolution of pulmonary hemorrhage. Bedside bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage performed; BALF and blood collected for genomic analysis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Severe pulmonary hemorrhagic leptospirosis presenting with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH), ultra-severe ARDS (P/F ratio 66 mmHg), profound thrombocytopenia (12 x 10^9/L), rhabdomyolysis (myoglobin >2000 ng/mL), and acute hepatic and renal dysfunction. Confirmed on day 3 by blood and BALF mNGS detecting Leptospira.
Plan & Treatment: Emergency endotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, VV-ECMO support for 255 hours (first 60 hours without UFH anticoagulation due to severe hemorrhage), continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), and intermittent prone positioning. Antimicrobial therapy: IV moxifloxacin (0.4 g daily) and IV imipenem/cilastatin (1 g q8h). High-dose pulse methylprednisolone (500 mg IV daily for 3 days), recombinant human thrombopoietin (15,000 U SC daily), platelet transfusion (10 U on day 4), fresh plasma, packed red blood cells, and norepinephrine infusion (0.1-1.2 mcg/kg/min).
Outcome: VV-ECMO successfully decannulated on day 11, extubated on day 15, transferred to step-down ward on day 17, and discharged home fully recovered on day 21.
